desk_summary: Built Sunday at your request. Lead: your Controversial Call (324 words), running long enough to take the lead and secondary space.

Checked on fie.org this morning: all four U.S. Vet Worlds women's medals hold, and the U.S. women also won the veterans team event (45-31 over France). Team names stay out because FIE and Wikipedia list different teams.
Elsayed is in as Secondary B: FIE's own ranking shows him No. 1 and the FIE article backs every line. By the Book is written from the October 2026 rulebook (unjustified appeals, t.172/t.174/t.165).

Club results: nothing new through Saturday. Two Elite FC cadets fence today's NJ Junior Olympics qualifier. The Monday pass adds them if they finish strong; otherwise they go on the 'also fenced' line.

Boards refreshed: Morris Cup still has 20 fencers and 30 entries; Ultimate Cup adds Anayaa Sheth (13 entries); Medeo #4/#5 is one line, pending entries included. Fill is about 69% with everything vetted, 74% with For the Parents, and about 75% once the JO results are in (No. 2 printed at about 78%). Stretch option: the Winter Camp flyer photo adds about 6%.

slots.title: Controversial Calls: The Touch Nobody Saw Land, Except the Referee
slots.summary: Your son's pool bout from two years ago: the touch the family says landed off the strip, the appeal and the Head Referee's ruling, what t.93, t.94.1 and t.172 say, both sides labeled as opinion, and the verdict: judgment call. It carries the editor's note and a short For Parents coda.

flags.text: Vetted as-is Oct. 13. Its 324 words are about double a normal lead, so it fills the Secondary A space too (your space-saving call).
No referee is named. Bout facts are attributed to the family. Rule cites are checked against the October 2026 rulebook.

slots.slot: Secondary A — Vet Worlds, part two
slots.summary: Follow-up to No. 2's men's item. Leslie Marx won Veteran 50 (10-4 final); Cassandra Bates took silver (10-9 final) and Lacey Biniak bronze in Veteran 40; Charlotta Bowie took bronze in Veteran 70. The U.S. also won the women's veterans team event. Every result is from fie.org, checked this morning.

flags.text: Team names left out: the FIE entry list shows Biniak, Buechel, Exum, Marchant and Martinez Hansen, but Wikipedia shows Bates, Biniak, Exum, Foellmer and Marx. The story says only 'the U.S. won'.
The FIE lists dates only, no start or end times. The women's events ran Oct. 12–14.

answered: Conditional vet from Frank, condition met (fie.org check 2026-10-18).

slots.slot: Secondary B — World No. 1's message to himself
slots.summary: Egypt's Mohamed Elsayed recorded a video promise to himself after Tokyo and kept it with a Paris 2024 bronze. He tells Ari Simmons the story on the FIE's 'Will to Win' podcast. The FIE ranking shows him No. 1 in men's epee.

flags.text: Written from the FIE's own article and ranking page only. Desk didn't listen to the episode. This is the first story to drop if space is tight.
